title: Flix Projected Concrete Syntax Tree Schema
description: Schema for projected concrete syntax trees produced from Flix source files against the pinned oracle. A document is one of two forms of the same parse, and `form` says which: `raw` is the reference's own tree, node for node, and `normalized` is that tree with ast/transparency.json's rules applied. Both are committed -- fixtures/raw/ and fixtures/expected/ -- because they answer different questions, and a projected tree whose shape depends on an unstated normalisation is not comparable to anything.

schemaVersion.description: 2: `form` became required, because there are now two committed forms of every parse and an unlabelled one cannot be placed. A reader that gated on version 1 was reading documents that had no normalisation applied at all; failing loudly is the intended outcome.

form.description: `raw` -- the producing parser's own tree, verbatim, with its wrappers and its error-recovery vocabulary intact. For the reference that is fixtures/raw/, the provenance record and the authority the recovery lane compares against; for a consumer it is the ordinary case, since the conformance comparison applies that consumer's declared transparency rules itself. `normalized` -- the canonical tree, with wrapper nodes elided and the error vocabulary spliced out per ast/transparency.json, which is what fixtures/expected/ holds and what a consumer is asked to agree with.

generatedBy.description: Fully qualified generator that produced this file.

toolVersion.description: Generator version; bumped when the emitted format changes.

upstreamCommit.description: flix/flix commit this projection was derived from.

oracleSha256.description: SHA-256 of the oracle jar actually used.

source.description: Repository-relative, forward-slashed path. Never absolute: committed expectations must not be machine-specific.

diagnostics.description: Lexer and parser diagnostics, sorted by (line, col, kind).

kind.description: Sub-trait-qualified TreeKind name drawn from ast/treekind.json, e.g. Expr.Apply. Bare names are ambiguous: 13 simple names are reused across sub-traits.

Diagnostic.description: kind and line are gated by conformance; col and message are advisory because both are recovery-dependent (implementation plan section 3.4).
